original_question: Must every graph with exactly three distinct adjacency eigenvalues have at most three distinct vertex degrees?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.6 in Section 3.2 ("Signed graphs with few eigenvalues"): "Does a graph with three distinct eigenvalues have at most three distinct degrees?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It correctly asks a universal question about graphs with exactly three distinct adjacency eigenvalues and asks whether this forces at most three distinct vertex degrees. It also correctly avoids adding connectivity, regularity, or bipartiteness assumptions that are not present in Problem 3.6 itself.
missing_details: The paper's Problem 3.6 is posed in the ordinary unsigned-graph setting, even though the paper as a whole is about signed graphs; that ambient setting should be made explicit in a stand-alone version.
The relevant eigenvalues are those of the adjacency matrix A(G); your draft suggests this by saying "adjacency eigenvalues," but a fully self-contained version should name the matrix.
To make the question stand-alone, it is helpful to state the standard graph-theoretic convention explicitly: G is a finite undirected graph (typically simple in this literature).
The paper's word "degrees" means the set of vertex degrees, equivalently valencies; spelling this out removes any ambiguity.
No extra hypothesis such as connectedness, regularity, or bipartiteness should be inserted: those appear only in the surrounding discussion and in the separate bipartite variant Problem 3.7.
refined_question: For a finite unsigned graph G with adjacency matrix A(G), if A(G) has exactly three distinct eigenvalues, must the set of vertex degrees of G have cardinality at most 3?
justification: The draft is essentially a faithful paraphrase of Problem 3.6. The nearby paragraph in Section 3.2 explicitly shifts to the unsigned-graph setting, discusses graphs with few adjacency eigenvalues, and then states De Caen's open problem in exactly this form. The only paper-critical clarification needed to make the question fully stand-alone is that this is an unsigned graph question about the adjacency spectrum, with "degrees" meaning vertex degrees/valencies. The separate immediately following Problem 3.7 confirms that one should not add connectedness or bipartiteness to Problem 3.6.
